html:
SMTO-UI-0047 — SMTO couldn't change the Gateways for this message

GUID: 3827d6d8-687c-4616-a9e2-f71794d7bf40
Slug: ui-gateway-selection-invalid
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • You picked a Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer) with @, but SMTO couldn't add it to or remove it from this message's targets. Your Gateway choices stayed as they were.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you just sent a message to a task that is still running, wait until that message is accepted before changing Gateways. SMTO locks the Gateway choice while a message to a running task is being delivered.
  2. Open the Gateway target menu under the message box, select Refresh targets, and check that the Gateway is listed and not shown as Disabled. A Gateway that was removed or switched off can't be added to a message.
  3. If 16 Gateways are already selected, select one you don't need in that menu to remove it, then add the new one. A message can target at most 16 Gateways.
  4. To use a disabled Gateway, turn it back on in Settings › Setup › Gateways, then select it again. Only enabled Gateways can be chosen as targets.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway appears as a chip under the message box, and the target menu shows it as selected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the Gateway you tried to add, to the person who manages your Gateways.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The @ mention palette could not add or remove the chosen Gateway because the target selector refused the change (a steer is in progress or the composer isn't ready, the Gateway is unknown or disabled, 16 are already selected, or it wasn't selected).

What this means

  • Gateway mention selection calls addGateway and the requested addition is not accepted by the current enabled selection rules. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway mention selection calls addGateway and the requested addition is not accepted by the current enabled selection rules.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect enabled records, the 16-target limit and primary selection before assuming a connection failure.

How to fix it

  • addGateway/removeGateway in agent_ui/target_selector.js return false when isSteering() is true (state.steerRequestId set or composer profile not ready), the gateway_id is absent from the loaded records or has status "disabled", or the selection already has MAX (16) entries; mention_palette.js then raises ui_gateway_selection_invalid. Refresh the Gateway records (Refresh targets / GET of the Gateway list), confirm the Gateway is enabled, and retry after the steer request settles.
  • Refresh the Gateway list and select up to 16 enabled Gateways, with one selected primary.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended enabled Gateway joins a valid selection with one primary.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
